See how you translated the similar expression in 3:16.

2.note: See how you translated **son of man** in [2:1](ta:02). This also occurs in verses 18 and 24.

Yahweh is using the question form for emphasis, to command Ezekiel to pronounce judgment on **the city of blood**. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [you must judge. Yes, you must pass judgment on the city of blood.]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **judge** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [will you surely judge]
Here, **blood** represents “murder.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the city of murderers]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **city** that is characterized by **blood**, that is, by murder. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the city whose people commit murder]

Yahweh is using the question form to command Ezekiel to confront the city with its sins. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And make her know all her abominations!]

The pronoun **her** refers to the city, and here it means the people who live in the city. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And you will make the people of the city know all their abominations]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **abominations**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the detestable things that she has done]
See how you translated the similar expression in [4:1](ta:04).

3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. This also occurs in verse 28. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell her that the Lord Yahweh says this]

Even though Yahweh is addressing the city directly, as the next verse shows, he is speaking of it in the third person as **A city** and **her**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [You are a city pouring blood in your midst, so that your time may come—and you have made idols against yourself, to become unclean]

Yahweh is using **pouring blood** as a common expression of the culture to mean “murdering people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [A city murdering people in her midst]

Yahweh is using **her time may come** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the time for her punishment may come.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [so that the time for her to be punished may come]

Yahweh is speaking of the city, which he calls **she**, as if it were a living thing that could make idols. He means the people who live in the city. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the people who live in her have made idols that harm themselves, so that they have become unclean]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if making idols had made the city ritually **unclean**. It means that the people of the city have become guilty and unacceptable to him because of their sin. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to become guilty and unacceptable to me]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:8. This also occurs in verses 19 and 28.

4.note: The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing the city of Jerusalem as a woman. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using **you have brought your days near, and you have come to your years** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you have caused the time of your punishment to come soon.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you have caused the time of your punishment to come soon, and the years of your judgment have arrived]

The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [So because of these things, I have given you]

The expressions **a reproach to the nations** and **a mockery to all the lands** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two expressions together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [as something that people everywhere utterly despise]

If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **reproach** and **mockery**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [over to the nations so that they will insult you and to all the lands so that they will ridicule you]

Here, **all the lands** represents “the people who live in all the lands.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the people of every country]

5.note: Yahweh is referring to all of the people in the world by naming two major components, people who are **near** and people who are **far from you**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [All the people of the world]

Yahweh is using the adjectives **near** and **far** as nouns to mean certain kinds of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [The nations that are near you and the nations that are far from you]

Yahweh is using the possessive form twice to describe the city. He means that its **name** is **unclean** and that it is full of **turmoil**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you whose name is unclean, you who are full of turmoil]
Here, **name** represents “reputation.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [you with your defiled reputation]

6.note: Here, **arm** represents “power.” Yahweh means that each of the princes uses his own power to murder people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [each man according to his own power]
Here, **in order to** marks **pour blood** as the goal or purpose of **they are in you**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. This also occurs in verse 9.

7.note: Yahweh is using **they have lightened** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they have treated with contempt.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Father and mother, they have treated with disrespect in you]

The pronoun **your** refers to the city of Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [toward the foreigner they have acted with oppression in the midst of Jerusalem]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **oppression**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [oppressively]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **fatherless** child or a specific **widow**. He means fatherless children and widows in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [fatherless children and widows]

8.note: In the previous verse Yahweh spoke of the princes in the third person as “they,” but here he speaks directly to the people of the city in the second person as **you**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make it clear that the speaker is now addressing the people of the city. Alternate translation: [My holy things you people of Jerusalem have despised]

9.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **Men** who are characterized by **slander**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Men who slander]

The implication is that these men have eaten sacrificial meals at shrines **on the mountains** as part of worshiping idols. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and in you, they have eaten sacrificial meals to idols at the shrines on the mountains]

10.note: Yahweh is referring to having sexual relations with one’s father’s wife in a polite way by using the phrase **The nakedness of a father, he has uncovered**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [A man has slept with his father’s wife in you]
The pronoun **he** refers to any man among the people of the city. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [some man among your people has uncovered in you]

Yahweh is referring to forcing a woman to have sexual relations during her monthly period in a polite way by using the phrase **the unclean** one **of menstruation, they have abused**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [they have forced themselves on women during their monthly periods]

Yahweh is using the adjective **unclean** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person, a woman who is ritually unclean because she is menstruating. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the woman who is unclean because of her menstruation]

11.note: Yahweh is referring to adultery in a polite way by using the phrase **with the wife of his neighbor, he has done an abomination**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [with the wife of his neighbor, he has committed adultery]

Yahweh is not distinguishing this **sister** from another sister who is not **the daughter of his father**. Yahweh is reminding his listeners that this woman is closely related to the man, since they have the same father. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [his sister, who is the daughter of his own father]

12.note: The terms **Interest** and **usury** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Much interest]

Yahweh is using **me, you have forgotten** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you have stopped obeying and worshiping me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you have stopped obeying and worshiping me]

Yahweh is using **the declaration of the Lord Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with his authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. This also occurs in verses 12 and 31.

13.note: Striking one’s palm was a symbolic action by which Yahweh showed that he was angry about what the people had done. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [I have struck my palm to show that I am angry]

Here, **blood** represents “the murders that you have committed.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and against the murders that you have committed in your midst]

14.note: Yahweh is using the question form for emphasis, to tell the people that they will not have courage or strength when he punishes them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Your heart will certainly not remain courageous, nor will your hands remain strong]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the courage of the people were a **heart** that could **stand** firm. It refers to remaining brave. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Will you remain brave]

Yahweh is using **will your hands be strong** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will you be able to resist.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will you be able to resist]

Yahweh is using **I am doing with you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I am punishing you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for the days when I am punishing you]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:15.

15.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will scatter you far and wide among the nations and the lands]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the **uncleanness** of the people were something that he could remove from them completely. It means that he will put an end to their sinful behavior. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will put a complete end to your sinful behavior]

If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **uncleanness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and I will completely remove from you what makes you unclean]

16.note: The expression **you will be profaned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And you will profane yourself in the eyes of the nations]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:8.
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:7. This also occurs in verse 22.

18.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Israel were **dross**, the worthless material that remains when metalworkers purify silver. It means that the people have become worthless to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the house of Israel has become worthless to me]

In this verse, the phrase **the house of Israel** is singular in form, but it refers to all the Israelites as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a plural form. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel have become to me as dross]

The term **dross** refers to a kind of waste material that metalworkers remove when they melt metal in order to purify it. If your readers would not be familiar with what dross is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. This also occurs in verse 19. Alternate translation: [like the useless scum that metalworkers skim off melted metal]

18.q: כֻּלָּ֡⁠ם נְ֠חֹשֶׁת וּ⁠בְדִ֨יל וּ⁠בַרְזֶ֤ל וְ⁠עוֹפֶ֨רֶת֙ בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ כּ֔וּר
18.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Israel were **bronze and tin and iron and lead in the midst of a furnace**, the less valuable metals that metalworkers separate from silver. It means that the people are impure and worthless to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All of them are impure and worthless to me]
See how you translated the similar expression in [3:1](ta:03).

19.note: Yahweh is using **behold me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I am about to.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to collect you]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people were metal that a metalworker is **collecting** into a furnace. It means that he will bring them together in Jerusalem in order to punish them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [gathering you together in Jerusalem in order to punish you]

20.q: קְבֻ֣צַת כֶּ֡סֶף וּ֠⁠נְחֹשֶׁת וּ⁠בַרְזֶ֨ל וְ⁠עוֹפֶ֤רֶת וּ⁠בְדִיל֙ אֶל תּ֣וֹךְ כּ֔וּר לָ⁠פַֽחַת עָלָ֥י⁠ו אֵ֖שׁ לְ⁠הַנְתִּ֑יךְ כֵּ֤ן אֶקְבֹּץ֙
20.note: The point of this comparison is that just as metalworkers collect **silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin into the midst of a furnace** in order **to melt** them, so Yahweh will collect the people into Jerusalem in order to punish them severely. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as metalworkers collect silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin into the midst of a furnace, to blow fire on it, to melt it, so I will collect you]

The expressions **in my nose** and **in my heat** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two expressions together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [in my burning anger]
Here, **nose** represents “anger.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in my anger]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his anger were **heat**. It means that he is very angry. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and in my great anger]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I will set you in the midst of the furnace]

21.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **wrath** were a fire that he could **blow on** the people, as a metalworker blows on a fire to make it hotter. It means that he will punish them severely because he is angry with them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will punish you severely because I am very angry with you]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **fire** that is characterized by his **wrath**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. This also occurs in verse 31. Alternate translation: [with the fire that expresses my wrath]

The expression **you will be melted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This also occurs in verse 22. Alternate translation: [and I will melt you in her midst]
The pronoun **her** refers to Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in the midst of Jerusalem]

22.q: כְּ⁠הִתּ֥וּךְ כֶּ֨סֶף֙ בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ כּ֔וּר כֵּ֖ן תֻּתְּכ֣וּ בְ⁠תוֹכָ֑⁠הּ
22.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **silver** is melted **in the midst of a furnace**, so the people will be **melted in her midst**, that is, punished severely in Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [I will punish you severely in the midst of Jerusalem, as severely as silver is melted in a furnace]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **heat**, meaning his anger, were a liquid that he had **poured** on the people. It means that he has punished them severely because he is angry with them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, have punished you severely because I am angry with you]

24.note: Even though Ezekiel is addressing the land directly as **You**, he speaks of it in the third person as **it**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [You are a land that has not been cleansed]

Here, **a land** represents “the people who live in the land.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [You people dwell in a land]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the sin of the people were dirt on the land that **has not been cleansed**. It means that the people have not been made free from their guilt. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [its people have not been freed from their guilt]

The expression **it has not been cleansed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [nobody has cleansed it]

The implication is that Yahweh will not send rain on the land during the time when he is punishing the people because he is angry with them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I will not send rain on her during the time when I punish her in my anger]
The pronoun **Her** refers to the land. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The rain of the land is]

Yahweh is using **the day of indignation** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the time when I punish her in my anger.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [during the time when I punish her in my anger]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **indignation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in the day when I am indignant]

25.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **conspiracy** that is formed by **her prophets**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Her prophets have formed a conspiracy in her midst]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a lion roaring, tearing prey** is violent and destructive, so are the prophets of Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [being violent and destructive like a lion roaring, tearing prey]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the prophets had **eaten** people the way a lion eats its prey. It means that they have killed people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They have killed people]

The terms **wealth** and **precious** things mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [all the valuable things they have taken]

The implication is that the prophets have caused there to be many widows in the city by killing their husbands. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [they have killed many husbands, multiplying her widows in her midst]

26.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **law** were a person whom the priests had attacked with **violence**. It means that the priests have disobeyed his law and have not taught it correctly. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Her priests have disobeyed my law and have not taught it correctly]

26.q: בֵּֽין קֹ֤דֶשׁ לְ⁠חֹל֙ לֹ֣א הִבְדִּ֔ילוּ וּ⁠בֵין הַ⁠טָּמֵ֥א לְ⁠טָה֖וֹר לֹ֣א הוֹדִ֑יעוּ
26.note: Yahweh is using the adjectives **holy**, **common**, **unclean**, and **clean** as nouns to mean certain kinds of things. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [Between what is holy and what is common, they have not separated, and between what is unclean and what is clean, they have not made known]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and they have not made known the difference between the unclean and the clean]

Yahweh is using **from my Sabbaths, they have hidden their eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they have refused to pay attention to my Sabbaths.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they have refused to pay attention to my Sabbaths]

The expression **I am profaned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [So they profane me in their midst]

27.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **wolves tearing prey** are violent and destructive, so are the princes of Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Her princes within her violently and destructively attack people]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this.

28.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the prophets were workers who covered a weak wall with **whitewash** to make it look strong. It means that the prophets have made the sins of the people seem acceptable by giving them false messages. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And her prophets have made the people’s sins seem acceptable]

The implication is that the prophets claim to have seen visions and to have learned the future through divination, but these visions and messages are false. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [claiming to see visions that are empty and practicing divination that gives them false messages]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **emptiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [envisioning things that are not real]
Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [but I have not spoken]

29.note: The implication is that **The people of the land** are the ordinary people of Israel, in contrast to the leaders whom Yahweh has already mentioned. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The ordinary people of Israel]

Yahweh is using constructions in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this.

Yahweh is using the adjectives **poor** and **needy** as nouns to mean certain kinds of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [and the poor people and the needy people they have wronged]

The terms **poor** and **needy** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and the extremely poor]

30.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the land were a city with a broken wall, and as if a person who would plead with him for the people were **a man walling up a wall and standing in the gap** to defend the city. It means that Yahweh looked for someone who would ask him not to destroy the land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a man defending the people and standing up for them]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [a person]
Here, **face** represents “presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before me]

31.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 21:31.

Yahweh is using **I have finished them** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I have completely destroyed them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have completely destroyed them]

Yahweh is using **Their way on their head I have given** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I have punished them as their conduct deserves.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have punished them as their conduct deserves]
